title.title: The Signal at Kestrel
title.premise: Audio archivist Mara Venn returns to remote Kestrel Island when its abandoned beacon broadcasts a recording of her missing sister.
title.rightsNote: An original fictional NoSpoilers demonstration. No third-party scripts, transcripts, plots, or characters were used.

shortRecap.text: Mara Venn returns to Kestrel Island after the abandoned beacon broadcasts her missing sister June’s recorded voice.
The message includes a phrase only the sisters used, and the supposedly disconnected beacon had power during an island outage.

longRecap.text: Audio archivist Mara Venn returns to Kestrel Island after its abandoned beacon transmits the voice of her sister June, who disappeared years earlier.
The transmission uses a private phrase from the sisters’ childhood, convincing Mara that the source drew on material connected to June.
Harbor mechanic Ellis Rook ferries Mara to the island, while archive director Dr. Sable Chen allows her to inspect the stored recordings.
The immediate unanswered problem is practical: the beacon broadcast while the island grid was down even though it was supposed to be disconnected.

shortRecap.text: Mara proves the transmission was spliced from June’s old field tapes, but nothing yet identifies who assembled it.
Salt marks on the equipment match an old buoy-maintenance map, and Toma Vale admits he heard a similar signal before Mara arrived.

longRecap.text: Mara’s audio analysis shows that the beacon message was assembled from fragments of June’s 2009 field recordings.
The splice establishes how June’s voice could be used, but the available material does not identify the person who made it.
Corrosion and salt traces on the beacon equipment correspond to a route on an old buoy-maintenance map.
Fisher Toma Vale admits he heard earlier bursts of the same signal and kept that from the others.
Sable tells Mara that June had been investigating altered rescue-call logs before she vanished.

shortRecap.text: Ellis admits he restored power to the beacon three weeks earlier after receiving a written request from Sable.
Mara confirms the broadcast is a recent construction from archived fragments, not a live transmission from June.

longRecap.text: Ellis admits that he quietly restored the beacon’s backup power three weeks before Mara returned.
He says he acted on a written equipment-test request bearing Sable’s name; the request establishes why Ellis was there, not who made the broadcast.
Mara’s waveform comparison confirms that the voice message is a recent edit built from archived recordings rather than live speech from June.
The open questions are who assembled the edit and why the buoy route appears in the physical evidence.

shortRecap.text: Mara traces the signal through the retired buoy network, and Toma gives her the field notebook he hid after June disappeared.
June’s notes say someone called “Grey Finch” altered rescue calls, but the material through episode 4 does not identify that person.

longRecap.text: Using the maintenance map and recorded delays, Mara traces the broadcast path through Kestrel’s retired buoy network.
Toma admits that he found and hid June’s field notebook after her disappearance because he feared it would be destroyed.
The notebook says a person using the name “Grey Finch” altered rescue-call logs. At this boundary, that name is not connected to an identified person.
Sable acknowledges that the buoy path was once used as a private salvage channel.
It is established that the new signal used old infrastructure and June’s archived audio; who assembled it and Grey Finch’s identity remain unresolved.

shortRecap.text: A signed maintenance authorization and June’s cipher key establish that Sable Chen used the name “Grey Finch.”
The altered calls concealed unauthorized salvage traffic, and June’s notes show she reached the sea tunnel while investigating it.

longRecap.text: Mara matches June’s notebook cipher to a maintenance authorization signed by Sable, establishing that Sable used the name “Grey Finch.”
The altered rescue-call records concealed unauthorized salvage traffic through the old buoy channel.
June’s decoded route notes show that she followed the traffic as far as the sea tunnel on the night she disappeared.
The origin of the recent broadcast and what happened after June entered the tunnel are still not established at this boundary.

shortRecap.text: June’s recovered recorder establishes that she escaped the tunnel and later chose to leave Kestrel under a new identity after documenting the salvage operation.
Toma assembled the recent beacon message from June’s tapes to force the sealed archive to reopen, and he gives Mara June’s final recording.

longRecap.text: A recorder recovered beyond the sea tunnel establishes that June escaped and documented the salvage operation.
June explains that she chose to leave Kestrel under a new identity after threats made a public return unsafe.
Toma admits that he constructed the recent beacon message from June’s archived field tapes so the closed archive would be investigated again.
He gives Mara June’s final recording, and Mara publishes the documented rescue-log and salvage evidence.

evidence.text: Mara Venn is an audio archivist and June Venn’s sister.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara identifies herself as an audio archivist when she requests access to June’s stored field tapes.

evidence.text: The abandoned beacon broadcasts a recording of June Venn’s voice.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: The beacon transmission contains a sentence spoken in June Venn’s recorded voice.

evidence.text: The message includes a private childhood phrase known to Mara and June.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara recognizes the phrase as one the sisters used privately as children.

evidence.text: The disconnected beacon had power during an island-wide outage; the available evidence does not yet explain how.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: The control panel logs power during the outage despite the beacon’s disconnected status.

evidence.text: Ellis Rook is Kestrel’s harbor mechanic and ferries Mara to the island.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Ellis introduces himself as the harbor mechanic before taking Mara across.

evidence.text: Dr. Sable Chen directs the Kestrel audio archive and grants Mara access to June’s recordings.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Sable opens the archive store and identifies herself as its director.

evidence.text: Mara knows the broadcast uses June’s voice and their private childhood phrase.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara recognizes both the voice and the phrase while listening at the beacon.

evidence.text: Ellis knows that the beacon’s control panel registered power during the outage.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Ellis reads the power log with Mara inside the beacon house.

evidence.text: Sable knows Mara has returned to examine June’s archive recordings.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Sable signs Mara into the archive and discusses the purpose of her visit.

evidence.text: Mara and June are sisters; June has been missing for years.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara refers to June as her sister and describes the unresolved disappearance.

evidence.text: Mara proves the transmission was recently spliced from June’s 2009 field tapes, but the maker is not identified.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Matching breath sounds and tape noise identify three separate 2009 recordings in the transmitted sentence.

evidence.text: Salt traces on the beacon equipment match stops on an old buoy-maintenance map.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara lays the corrosion samples beside the maintenance chart and matches their mineral profiles.

evidence.text: Toma Vale is a fisher who heard earlier bursts of the same beacon signal and initially kept quiet about them.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Toma says his radio picked up two earlier bursts and admits he told no one.

evidence.text: Sable says June was investigating altered rescue-call logs before her disappearance.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Sable shows Mara a log discrepancy June had marked before she vanished.

evidence.text: Mara knows the message is a splice made from June’s old field tapes and that the equipment carries buoy-route salt traces.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara completes the audio and corrosion comparisons herself.

evidence.text: Toma knows the beacon signal was transmitted at least twice before Mara returned.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Toma heard and logged the earlier bursts on his fishing radio.

evidence.text: Sable knows June had marked alterations in the rescue-call logs.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Sable retrieves the page containing June’s handwritten discrepancy marks.

evidence.text: Ellis admits he restored the beacon’s backup power three weeks before Mara returned.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Ellis shows Mara his dated work log for the beacon generator repair.

evidence.text: Ellis says a written equipment-test request bearing Sable’s name prompted the repair.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: The work order shown on screen bears Sable’s printed name and archive office code.

evidence.text: Mara confirms the beacon message is a recent edit of archived fragments, not live speech from June.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: The splice software timestamps the edit format years after June’s disappearance.

evidence.text: Ellis knows he restored the backup power and that his work order bore Sable’s name.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Ellis describes the repair and hands the work order to Mara.

evidence.text: Sable knows that a beacon repair request carries her name and office code.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara shows Sable the signed work order during their archive conversation.

evidence.text: Mara traces the recent signal through Kestrel’s retired buoy network.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Signal delays and salt profiles align at each retired buoy on the route.

evidence.text: Toma reveals that he hid June’s field notebook after her disappearance because he feared it would be destroyed.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Toma retrieves the notebook from a sealed compartment beneath his boat.

evidence.text: Grey Finch is an unidentified name in June’s notebook associated with altered rescue calls; the material through episode 4 does not identify a person behind it.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: June’s note reads: Grey Finch changed the calls. No real name is attached to the entry.

evidence.text: Sable acknowledges that the retired buoy route once served as a private salvage channel.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Sable identifies the route on the map as an old channel used by salvage crews.

evidence.text: Mara knows the signal used the retired buoy route and that June’s notebook links the unidentified Grey Finch to altered rescue calls.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara completes the route trace and reads the Grey Finch entry.

evidence.text: Toma knows where June’s notebook was hidden and that it names Grey Finch without identifying that person.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Toma explains when he found the notebook and says he never decoded the name.

evidence.text: Sable knows Mara has traced the signal through the former salvage channel and obtained June’s notebook.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara shows Sable the route and notebook during their confrontation.

evidence.text: The signed authorization and June’s cipher key establish that Sable Chen used the name Grey Finch.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: The decoded initials on the authorization match Sable’s archive cipher and signature.

evidence.text: Sable altered rescue-call records to conceal unauthorized salvage traffic through the buoy channel.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: The decoded ledger aligns each altered call with an unlicensed salvage movement.

evidence.text: June’s decoded route notes establish that she reached the sea tunnel while investigating the salvage traffic.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: June’s final route mark before the notes stop is inside the sea tunnel.

evidence.text: Mara knows Sable used the name Grey Finch, why the rescue logs were altered, and that June reached the sea tunnel.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara decodes the notebook, authorization, and route marks together.

evidence.text: Sable knows Mara has connected her to the Grey Finch name and the altered rescue-call records.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara presents the decoded authorization and ledger to Sable.

evidence.text: June escaped the sea tunnel and chose to leave Kestrel under a new identity after documenting the salvage operation.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: June explains her escape and decision in the recovered recorder entry.

evidence.text: Toma assembled the recent beacon broadcast from June’s archived tapes to force the sealed archive to reopen.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Toma demonstrates the tape edits and explains why he sent the signal.

evidence.text: Toma gives Mara June’s final recording, and Mara publishes the documented rescue-log and salvage evidence.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara receives the recorder and releases the archive with its supporting records.

evidence.text: Toma knows he built the broadcast and that June’s final recorder establishes her escape.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Toma confesses beside the recovered recorder.

evidence.text: Mara knows June escaped, Toma made the recent broadcast, and the archive evidence is ready to publish.
evidence.sourceExcerpt: Mara listens to June’s recorder and receives Toma’s confession.
